I have been working this land for over fifty years. My father farmed it before me. I know the soils here in Quzhou — mostly alluvial loam, decent water-holding but needs replenishing every year. The wheat-maize rotation is the backbone of what I do, as it has been for decades. Millet I keep on the side plots — the soil there is lighter, and millet suits it. My boys work in the city so I cannot rely on heavy manual labor at peak times. I have to be efficient.

**Wheat:** I plant every October on about 20 mu. I have used the improved semi-dwarf varieties for years — better lodging resistance, higher yield. I will apply base fertilizer at plowing, then a topdress at jointing. Three irrigations: the winter water before freeze, jointing, and heading. That is my standard. Powdery mildew and stripe rust are the risks here — two fungicide passes, one herbicide early. I plough deep in autumn to break the hardpan.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in June, I seed directly into the stubble on the same 20 mu. Hybrid seed —郑单958 or similar. No-till this year to save labor and keep moisture. Two irrigations unless summer rains are good, but I do not count on them being enough. Topdress nitrogen at V6. One herbicide, one pass for corn borer if needed.

**Millet:** The other 10.4 mu. Spring planting, rotary tillage. I use a locally adapted improved variety — better yield than the old landrace but still suits the lighter soil. Millet does not need much water or nitrogen, which is why I keep it. Two irrigations. One herbicide pass. Minimal pesticide otherwise.

With family off-farm, I watch input costs carefully. I do not overapply — I have seen neighbors burn their fields with excess urea. My yields are steady and that is what matters at my age.
